patch.value: Recovery closure: the fraction of refusals an agent can act on using only the refusal becomes a measured, ratcheted gate

Every read surface in this product is contracted, budgeted, projected and gated. The surface an agent meets when it is wrong is none of those things, and it is the surface an agent meets most often while it is learning the tool. This feature makes recovery a measured property with a target, rather than a quality that individual error messages happen to have.

Definition. Recovery closure is the fraction of refusals from which a correct next invocation is derivable using only the refusal envelope, with no access to help output, documentation, source, or a second command. It is a single number over a replayable corpus, it has a natural target of one, and it degrades observably the moment a new surface ships without its domain.

Why it is worth building rather than fixing case by case. The 2026-08-01 measurement found thirteen of fifteen closed value domains fully teachable and two not, and the two failures were the field projection selector and the context intent selector, which are precisely the two flags that exist to make a read cheap. That distribution is not a coincidence of authorship, it is what happens when nothing measures the property: the surfaces that were written last, under the cost programme, did not inherit the behavior the older surfaces have. Without a number, the next cost lever will arrive the same way.

Scope, in three parts.

Part one, the corpus. A replayable set of wrong invocations covering, at minimum, every flag with a contract-declared closed domain, every subcommand family, every required-argument omission, and every mutually exclusive flag pair. The corpus is generated from the contract tables rather than hand-written, so it grows with the surface instead of drifting behind it, and it must include at least one case per declared error code so that a code with no reachable input is visible as such.

Part two, the scorer. A refusal is scored recoverable when the envelope mechanically yields a legal alternative: the complete legal domain, or a suggested retry that is itself legal, or an explicit statement that the value space is open. A single nearest-match suggestion does not score recoverable on its own, because it tells an agent what to try next without telling it what the domain is, and the difference appears the moment the first suggestion is also wrong. The scorer reports the closure fraction plus the list of unrecoverable cases.

Part three, the gate. The closure fraction becomes a ratchet in the same registry that owns every other gate: it may not fall, and a new command or flag that ships an unrecoverable refusal fails the build. A negative control proves the gate can fail.

Consequences that follow, deliberately in scope. The refusal envelope acquires a declared shape with the same discipline read envelopes already have, which is the prerequisite for any of this being machine-consumable. The exit code becomes part of that contract, because in a pipeline it is the only channel a shell reads. And the refusal becomes an input to context assembly rather than a terminal event, which is recorded in the context catalog under the slug refusal-conditioned-retrieval-repair and is downstream of this work.

Boundary. This feature owns the metric, the corpus, the scorer and the gate. It does not own the error-code taxonomy, which is a separate open item, nor the output-envelope grammar, which is another, nor tokens-per-completed-task replay, which measures success paths rather than failure paths. It consumes all three and duplicates none of them.

A replay corpus of wrong invocations is generated from the contract tables and covers every flag with a closed domain, every subcommand family, every required-argument omission and every mutually exclusive flag pair; Every declared error code is reachable from at least one corpus input, and a code with no reachable input is reported as such; A scorer reports the recovery-closure fraction and the list of unrecoverable refusals, scoring a lone nearest-match suggestion as not recoverable; The closure fraction is a ratchet in the gate registry that may not fall, with a negative control proving the gate can fail; The refusal envelope has a declared shape carrying the failing surface, the rejected value, the legal domain when known, and the exit code
